# Collector relocation sketch

An early, unfinished sketch of what moving the valley-bottom collector to a
different site further up the slope would actually involve, written up
because the idea keeps coming up in conversation without anyone having
worked through what it would cost or whether it would even help. Nothing
here has been decided, and the gated status is there so this doesn't get
mistaken for an agreed plan.

## Why moving it is even on the table

The current collector sits at the low point of the valley, which made sense
when it was placed there for cable-run reasons early on, but the low point
is also where cold air pools on clear nights and where the radio hops from
the western stations have the worst margin, since every hop into the
collector from that side is effectively climbing out of a dip. Moving the
collector partway up the eastern slope would shorten and flatten several of
those hops at once, rather than fixing them one at a time.

## What a move up-slope would actually involve

Every station currently pointed at the collector's existing radio would
need its antenna re-aimed, which is a full round of site visits rather than
a single afternoon's work, and a couple of the western stations might need
an intermediate repeater hop added if the new angle turns out to be worse
for them even though it's better for the eastern side. Power at a new site
is the open question mark — the current collector site has mains behind it
from the adjacent building, and nothing up-slope does, so a relocated
collector would likely need to run off solar and battery like the stations
themselves, which is a different reliability profile than what it has now.

## What's been looked at so far

A rough walk of two candidate spots partway up the eastern slope, neither
surveyed properly, just eyeballed for line of sight back down to the
stations that currently struggle. Both looked plausible from where I stood,
but "looked plausible standing there for ten minutes" is a long way from a
proper site survey with a spectrum check and a look at ground access for a
solar panel and battery box.

## What's still completely open

Whether the radio improvement is even worth the cost of a full re-aim round
and a new power setup hasn't been weighed against just adding a repeater at
the current low-point site, which would fix the same hop problem without
moving anything. No cost estimate exists for either option. Nobody has
raised this with the landowner at either candidate site, so even the most
promising spot on paper might not be available at all. This stays a sketch,
not a proposal, until at least the repeater alternative has been costed out
properly alongside it.
